spec_facts.statement: FIPS 203 defines the ring R_q as Z_q[X]/(X^n + 1), with n = 256 and q = 3329, and represents an element f of R_q as a length-256 coefficient array (f_0, ..., f_255) in Z_q^256.

evidence_references.excerpt: n denotes 256; q denotes 3329; R_q = Z_q[X]/(X^n + 1); an element f = f_0 + ... + f_255 X^255 is represented by (f_0,...,f_255) in Z_q^256 and f[i] = f_i.
evidence_references.supports_claim: R_q, n, q, and the coefficient-array representation of a polynomial.

spec_facts.statement: FIPS 203 defines T_q as the image of R_q under the NTT; elements of T_q are called NTT representations of polynomials in R_q, and are represented in pseudocode as length-256 arrays of integers modulo q.
spec_facts.verification_relevance: candidate algorithm-to-code cross-reference for NTT-domain polynomial addition inputs and outputs.

evidence_references.excerpt: T_q is the image of R_q under the NTT; an NTT representation is a tuple of 128 degree-one polynomials, represented as a length-256 array in Z_q^256 with g[2i]=g_{i,0} and g[2i+1]=g_{i,1}.
evidence_references.supports_claim: Definition and representation of T_q elements.

spec_facts.statement: The standard states that the algebraic operations of addition and scalar multiplication in R_q and T_q are done coordinate-wise, and that addition of two NTT representations is performed in pseudocode by a statement of the form ĥ ← f̂ + ĝ.
spec_facts.verification_relevance: candidate algorithmic meaning for later addition correctness and per-coefficient assertions.

evidence_references.excerpt: Addition and scalar multiplication in R_q and T_q are done coordinate-wise; the addition of two NTT representations in pseudocode is performed by ĥ ← f̂ + ĝ.

spec_facts.statement: The standard interprets array operations on Z_m^ℓ as coordinate-wise: Z ← a·X and W ← X + Y produce arrays whose entries satisfy Z[i] = a·X[i] and W[i] = X[i] + Y[i] for all i.
